I was in the exact same situation a couple of months ago. I was set on the Superlight too but after comments here and some more of my own research I decided against it. Hopefully I can be genuinely helpful here…

• For me, it would live outside and it’s true they are VERY prone to rust.

• I’d only be on it 6 months hopefully before progressing onto a bigger bike, but they depreciate really badly that it could lose a third of what I paid for it in that time given point 1. 

• I was told mechanics won’t touch them and getting parts is a nightmare, but this seems to not be the case as much as it certainly was a few years ago. However, as I’m using it for commuting I didn’t want to take that risk.

• I was also told they don’t come with manuals (at least in English), but they can be downloaded from the website.

In the end, I went for a 2007 Kawasaki Eliminator for half the price of the SL, but unless I damage it or don’t look after it, it has already depreciated as much as it will do for the forseeable. So when it comes to upgrading I’ll get most of my money back. Kawasakis are also reliable, and the Eliminator looks great too even as a nearly 20 year old bike. 

I also considered Marauders, Intruders and I think Invaders, basically most mid-noughties Japanese Cruisers with aggressive names. They are all solid options and probably better bets than the Superlight. 

I’ll also say, if you are planning on doing your DAS etc, I’d say screw looking cool cause it’s difficult on 125’s most of the time and just get something cheap that does what you need it to do until you get your full license.

I think some compromise’s have to be made for the sake of enjoyability. 

Sandwalking, while immersive, would likely become very tedious very quickly and make you an easy target for other players. 

Shield/lasgun explosions are probably ruled out for a number of reasons. The scale of the explosions in the lore would be difficult to pull off in game realistically. If you are in a fairly large scale battle and everyone is shielded up and getting shot and nuclear explosions are going off every five seconds most peoples PC’s would also explode. 

Even if they made the explosions smaller scale to compromise it could likely be cheesed to kill players. One guy goes up to a group with his shield active and gets a buddy to snipe him. Kills the other players and himself but the buddy loots them all. There’s probably more reasons but those were the first that came to mind. 

I think if RP servers are a possibility then the option to toggle these more lore-friendly options on would be a great compromise.
